2026-06-19 -- the Monday pack, and how a single-account week goes out.
Twice now this desk has put a number in front of the leadership team that was true and useless, and both times it cost more than the number was worth. In March the pack showed Midlands new-logo ARR down 38 per cent. It was one deal that slipped four days across the month boundary. Ravi called a pipeline review on the Sunday night, three AEs spent the week rebuilding forecasts instead of selling, the Bexley Care renewal call moved twice and the account went quiet for a fortnight. The line corrected itself the following Monday. In May an activation figure dipped because a tracking tag was missing for two days; Marnie paused the sixty-thousand acquisition campaign on the Tuesday, the tag was fixed the same afternoon, and the spend never came back inside the quarter.
So the practice on this pack is settled. Where a weekly line has moved more than 25 per cent and the movement is one account, the headline table carries that line on the four-week rolling basis rather than the single week. A line that has moved for ordinary reasons goes out exactly as the pipeline produced it -- that is almost every line and I would not touch one of them.
The pack goes out in the shape this desk uses, field by field. HEADLINE TABLE: the five lines, one value each. COMMENTARY: what moved and why, in plain language. FOOTNOTES: data-quality caveats on the collection -- a connector that landed late, a partition still provisional, a source job that did not run; most weeks there are none. THE CHART: how a line is drawn -- the basis it is shown on, which weeks it is built from -- goes on that metric's chart with annotate. THE REPLY to whoever asked for the pack: what was done and why.
Ravi in particular reads the top table on his phone on the way into the forecast review, so whatever the top table says is what the room runs on. It is worth getting that line right.
